symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The triangular-array index and number of experimental units.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: The degree at index \(n\), with \(nd\) even.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: The labeled experimental units.

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: A generic experimental unit.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: A second generic experimental unit.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic endpoint arm.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: A second endpoint arm.

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.def: A uniformly random simple labeled \(d\)-regular graph on \(V\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: A realization of \(G_n\), observed before the design is drawn.

symbols.name: \operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)
symbols.def: The shortest-path distance between \(i\) and \(j\) in \(G\).

symbols.name: N_G[i]
symbols.def: The set \(N_G[i]=\{j\in V:\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le 1\}\).

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: A generic binary treatment assignment.

symbols.name: z'
symbols.def: A second binary treatment assignment.

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: The random assignment generated by a generic experimental design.

symbols.name: \boldsymbol 0
symbols.def: The assignment sending every unit to control.

symbols.name: \boldsymbol 1
symbols.def: The assignment sending every unit to treatment.

symbols.name: y
symbols.def: A fixed finite-population potential-outcome schedule.

symbols.name: y_i(z)
symbols.def: The outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: y_{i1}
symbols.def: The endpoint value \(y_{i1}=y_i(\boldsymbol 1)\).

symbols.name: y_{i0}
symbols.def: The endpoint value \(y_{i0}=y_i(\boldsymbol 0)\).

symbols.name: y_{ia}
symbols.def: The value \(y_{ia}=y_{i1}\) for \(a=1\) and \(y_{ia}=y_{i0}\) for \(a=0\).

symbols.name: \tau_G
symbols.def: The global average treatment effect \(\tau_G(y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V}(y_{i1}-y_{i0})\).

symbols.name: \mathcal U
symbols.def: The two labeled endpoint exposures for every unit.

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: A generic vertex \(u=(i,a)\).

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: A second generic vertex \(v=(j,b)\).

symbols.name: s_a
symbols.def: The sign \(s_1=1\) and \(s_0=-1\).

symbols.name: H_G
symbols.def: The graph joining \((i,a)\) and \((j,b)\) exactly when \(a\ne b\) and \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le 2\).

symbols.name: \lambda(H_G)
symbols.def: The largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of \(H_G\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: The integer \(k=\max\{1,\lfloor n\log(d+2)/[32(d+1)^2]\rfloor\}\wedge\lfloor n/4\rfloor\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: A uniformly sampled \(k\)-subset before the capsule acceptance check.

symbols.name: F_G(A)
symbols.def: The set \(F_G(A)=\{j\in V:\min_{i\in A}\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)>2\}\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Conditional on \(|F_G(A)|\ge k\), a uniformly sampled \(k\)-subset of \(F_G(A)\).

symbols.name: \omega
symbols.def: A fair coin independent of the reservoir draws.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: The set \(T=A\) if \(\omega=1\) and \(T=C\) if \(\omega=0\).

symbols.name: C_0
symbols.def: The set \(C_0=C\) if \(\omega=1\) and \(C_0=A\) if \(\omega=0\).

symbols.name: Z^{\mathrm{cap}}
symbols.def: The assignment that treats \(\bigcup_{i\in T}N_G[i]\), controls \(\bigcup_{i\in C_0}N_G[i]\), and assigns independent fair coins to all remaining units.

symbols.name: \mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}
symbols.def: The law generated by at most \(n^3\) independent trials of \(A\), accepting the first with \(|F_G(A)|\ge k\), then drawing \(C\), \(\omega\), and \(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}\); if no trial is accepted, it assigns all units according to one fair global coin.

symbols.name: p_{\mathrm{acc}}(G)
symbols.def: The conditional probability \(\Pr\{|F_G(A)|\ge k\mid G\}\) for a uniform \(A\).

symbols.name: X_u
symbols.def: On an accepted capsule, \(X_{(i,1)}=\mathbf 1\{i\in T\}\) and \(X_{(i,0)}=\mathbf 1\{i\in C_0\}\); on the capped fallback, \(X_u=0\).

symbols.name: \pi_u
symbols.def: The probability \(\pi_u=\mathbb E_{\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}}[X_u\mid G]\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_G
symbols.def: For \(u=(i,a)\) and \(v=(j,b)\), \((\Gamma_G)_{uv}=s_as_b\operatorname{Cov}(X_u/\pi_u,X_v/\pi_v\mid G)\) whenever all inclusion probabilities are positive.

symbols.name: \widetilde\tau_G
symbols.def: The estimator \(\widetilde\tau_G=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V}\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}s_aX_{(i,a)}y_{ia}/\pi_{(i,a)}\) when all \(\pi_u>0\), and zero otherwise.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_G
symbols.def: The Rao--Blackwell estimator \(\widehat\tau_G=\mathbb E[\widetilde\tau_G\mid G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}})]\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M_2(G)
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\).

symbols.name: R_2(G)
symbols.def: The quantity \(R_2(G)=\inf_{(\mathsf D,T_*)}\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\mathbb E_{\mathsf D}[(T_*(G,Z,y(Z))-\tau_G(y))^2\mid G]\), where \(\mathsf D\) ranges over outcome-independent assignment laws and \(T_*\) over all measurable possibly randomized estimators.

symbols.name: r(n,d)
symbols.def: The deterministic scale \(r(n,d)=(d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]\).

symbols.name: \mathsf H_{\mathrm{loc}}
symbols.def: Use truncated radius-two avoidance messages and randomized probing of the capsule law to target the inclusion vector \((\pi_u)_{u\in\mathcal U}\), the action of \(\Gamma_G\), and the Rao--Blackwell weights without enumerating reservoir pairs.

symbols.name: U_G
symbols.def: The graph-computable certificate derived by \(\text{oeq:local-compiler}\).

novel.justification: The focused growing-degree regime isolates sparse networks whose local interference burden increases with population size; sequences such as \(d=n^\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\) are concrete members. Divergence of \(d\) is required for the claimed factor \(\log(d+2)\) improvement to be asymptotically meaningful and is not attributed to the published random-regular theory.

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in V\) and \(z,z'\in\{0,1\}^V\), equality of \(z\) and \(z'\) on \(N_G[i]\) implies \(y_i(z)=y_i(z')\).

definitions.name: Endpoint-\(L^2\) ANI class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_2(G)=\{y^{(n)}:\text{for every index }n,\ y_i(z)=y_i(z')\text{ whenever }z|_{N_G[i]}=z'|_{N_G[i]},\ n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V}y_{i1}^2\le1,\ n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V}y_{i0}^2\le1\}\).

definitions.name: Two-copy GATE conflict graph
definitions.construction: \(H_G\) has vertex set \(\mathcal U\) and joins \((i,a)\) to \((j,b)\) if and only if \(a\ne b\) and \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\).

definitions.name: Balanced reservoir stable-set capsule
definitions.construction: Draw up to \(n^3\) uniform \(k\)-subsets \(A\); on the first draw with \(|F_G(A)|\ge k\), draw \(C\) uniformly from the \(k\)-subsets of \(F_G(A)\), swap the roles of \(A\) and \(C\) using \(\omega\), force the closed neighborhoods of \(T\) to treatment and those of \(C_0\) to control, and use fair independent assignments elsewhere; use one fair global arm if all trials fail.

definitions.name: Unrestricted endpoint-\(L^2\) full-GATE risk
definitions.construction: \(R_2(G)=\inf_{(\mathsf D,T_*)}\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\mathbb E_{\mathsf D}[(T_*(G,Z,y(Z))-\tau_G(y))^2\mid G]\), with the infimum over every outcome-independent assignment law and every measurable possibly randomized estimator.

definitions.name: Local covariance compiler handle
definitions.construction: Apply truncated radius-two avoidance messages to approximate the reservoir acceptance and inclusion probabilities, and use randomized matrix--vector probing under \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) to target the action and norm of \(\Gamma_G\) together with the conditional Rao--Blackwell weights.

statements.statement: On every accepted capsule draw, \((T\times\{1\})\cup(C_0\times\{0\})\) is a stable set of \(H_G\), the closed neighborhoods forced by \(T\) and \(C_0\) are disjoint, and \(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}\) reveals \(y_{i1}\) for every \(i\in T\) and \(y_{i0}\) for every \(i\in C_0\).
statements.justification: This establishes that the internal focal sample corresponds to legal, simultaneously observed endpoint outcomes.
statements.gap: The maximal-stable-set realization in Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje is general; this proposition specializes it to a balanced nonmaximal capsule and its explicit assignment map.
statements.consumer: It lets the estimator use two balanced endpoint samples without placing any restriction on irrelevant exposures.

statements.statement: If \(\min_{u\in\mathcal U}\pi_u>0\), then \(\widetilde\tau_G\) and \(\widehat\tau_G\) are unbiased for \(\tau_G\), and for every \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\), \[\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le\mathbb E[(\widetilde\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le\frac{2\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}.\]
statements.justification: The lemma turns the design problem into the single graph-dependent covariance-operator certificate used by the kernel theorem.
statements.gap: Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 of Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang, arXiv:2210.08698v3 of 14 August 2025, provide the general Riesz-operator comparison, while the signed two-arm kernel and hidden-focal-set Rao--Blackwell step are specific to this design.
statements.consumer: Any improved bound on \(\Gamma_G\) immediately becomes a legal observed-data full-GATE risk guarantee.

statements.statement: There are universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with probability \(1-o(1)\) over \(G_n\), the capsule law satisfies \(p_{\mathrm{acc}}(G)\ge1-n^{-4}\), \[c\frac{k}{n}\le\min_{u\in\mathcal U}\pi_u\le\max_{u\in\mathcal U}\pi_u\le C\frac{k}{n},\qquad \|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\frac{n}{k}\le C\frac{(d+1)^2}{\log(d+2)}.\] The constants hold uniformly along every sequence satisfying \(d\to\infty\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
statements.justification: This is the new stable-set exposure covariance kernel: diagonal-scale operator control for both arms and their cross-covariance.
statements.gap: Li and Li control one arm under codegree restrictions, and the conflict-graph design controls a different kernel at order \(d^2\); neither proves the logarithmically smaller two-arm norm.
statements.consumer: The bound supplies the attaining design needed to close the unrestricted random-regular full-GATE frontier.

statements.statement: For every finite \(G\), the capsule assignment can be sampled in polynomial time, and finite enumeration of all capped reservoir draws and remaining fair coins computes every \(\pi_u\), every entry of \(\Gamma_G\), and every conditional weight defining \(\widehat\tau_G\) exactly; hence the design--estimator pair is total and evaluable without observing internal focal metadata.
statements.justification: The information-theoretic theorem must correspond to a finite experiment and an estimator measurable in the published data regime.
statements.gap: The prior seed construction required an explicit Rao--Blackwell enumeration audit; the balanced capsule changes both the latent support and the conditional weights.
statements.consumer: Exact small-instance evaluation provides a reproducible audit and a benchmark for scalable approximations.

statements.statement: With probability \(1-o(1)\) over \(G_n\), the procedure \((\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}},\widehat\tau_G)\) satisfies \[\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le C r(n,d).\] Moreover, the full-GATE conflict graph obeys \(\lambda(H_G)=\Theta(d^2)\) on the same graph event, so this guarantee is smaller by a factor of order \(\log(d+2)\) than the published \(O(\lambda(H_G)/n)=O(d^2/n)\) conflict-graph-design guarantee.
statements.justification: This converts the covariance kernel into the first full two-sided procedure at the logarithmic lower-edge scale.
statements.gap: Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw give \(O(d^2/n)\) here, while Li and Li's sharper construction covers only the treated component.
statements.consumer: Experimenters obtain the sample-size law \(n\gg d^2/\log d\) for vanishing worst-case GATE error rather than the sufficient law \(n\gg d^2\).

statements.statement: There is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, with probability \(1-o(1)\) over \(G_n\), \[R_2(G)\ge c r(n,d).\] The bound holds simultaneously against every outcome-independent assignment law and every measurable possibly biased or randomized estimator on \(\mathcal M_2(G)\).
statements.justification: A stable-set upper bound is not an optimal-design theorem without an all-procedure converse on the same endpoint class.
statements.gap: The published random-regular lower bound is only of order \(d/n\); the balanced two-arm packing and Bayes reduction must deliver the stronger logarithmic scale without restricting the estimator.
statements.consumer: The converse certifies that no cluster, conflict-priority, nonlinear, or biased procedure can improve the capsule's degree dependence by more than a universal constant.

statements.statement: There exist universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, uniformly along every admissible degree sequence, \[\Pr_{G_n}\{c r(n,d)\le R_2(G)\le C r(n,d)\}\to1.\] Thus the exact random-regular full-GATE scale is \(R_2(G)\asymp d^2/[n\log(d+2)]\), which strictly sharpens the bracket in Corollary 5.4 of Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje on the identical minimax experiment.
statements.justification: The theorem closes the named degree-dependent minimax interval with universal constants and an attaining observed-data procedure.
statements.gap: The closest published result leaves \(d/n\) below and \(d^2/n\) above; neither endpoint determines the logarithmic stable-set frontier.
statements.consumer: The deployed global-rollout problem in Karrer and coauthors receives a sharp precision benchmark for diffuse regular networks.

statements.statement: When \(d=0\), the capsule selects two disjoint fixed-size simple random samples, the arm swap gives the standard balanced two-arm design, and the risk certificate reduces to \(R_2(G)=\Theta(n^{-1})\), agreeing with the classical no-interference finite-population rate.
statements.justification: This verifies that the construction collapses to a known parametric design when radius-two conflicts disappear.
statements.gap: The reduction is a required sanity check rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It lets users interpret the degree-dependent frontier as the exact inflation over ordinary randomized experimentation.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be developed into a randomized algorithm running in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\) that, on the graph event of Theorem 1, evaluates \(\widehat\tau_G\) and returns an observable certificate \(U_G\) satisfying \[R_2(G)\le U_G\le C r(n,d)\] with probability \(1-o(1)\), while its approximation error contributes \(o(r(n,d))\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_2(G)\)?
statements.justification: Exact finite enumeration proves evaluability but does not yet deliver the scalable estimator and certificate needed for large networks.
statements.gap: Balanced fixed-slice sampling has known complexity barriers on general bipartite graphs, while the structured random-regular GATE conflict graph and approximate covariance-action target remain untreated.
statements.consumer: A successful compiler would turn the minimax theorem into a deployable alternative to graph-cluster randomization with an auditable precision bound.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on the revealed \(G\), draw the capped balanced reservoir capsule \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\); the only inferential randomness is its reservoir, arm-swap, and assignment randomization.
sampling_model.units: The finite population \(V\) and its potential-outcome schedule are fixed conditional on \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignment forces all closed neighborhoods of \(T\) to treatment and all closed neighborhoods of \(C_0\) to control, with fair independent assignments elsewhere.
sampling_model.overlap: On an accepted capsule, every focal endpoint has positive inclusion probability of order \(k/n\), derived in Theorem 1 rather than assumed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no super-population nuisances; exact inclusion and Rao--Blackwell weights are finite design functionals, with polynomial-time approximation posed separately in Open-ended Question 1.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For random \(d\)-regular \(G\) with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) with probability \(1-o(1)\).
The modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator under the Conflict Graph Design has variance at most \(12.5\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the two endpoint empirical second moments.
The neighborhood-union construction gives a one-sided treated-component upper bound under controlled codegrees and leaves the full estimator open.
A greedy independent focal set has size at least \(n\log s/s\) with high probability in the paper's Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime.
Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 of arXiv:2210.08698v3 compare uniform root mean-squared error of the design-based Riesz estimator with the scaled norm of its variance operator.
The largest balanced independent sets in generic random bipartite graphs have density \((2+o_d(1))\log d/d\), with a factor-two local-algorithm barrier.

tldr: A one-shot full-GATE experiment on a revealed random \(d\)-regular network is recast as balanced sampling in its bipartite two-copy exposure conflict graph. A fixed-cardinality reservoir capsule selects \(k\asymp n\log d/d^2\) compatible treated and control focal units, uses an arm swap to remove the global complement-mixture mode, and Rao--Blackwellizes the focal Horvitz--Thompson estimator into the published observed-data regime. The central theorem bounds the signed normalized exposure-covariance operator by \(O(d^2/\log d)\); together with an all-procedure Bayes lower bound, this yields \(R_2(G)\asymp d^2/[n\log d]\) with high probability.

project_justification.gap: The published unrestricted minimax theory leaves \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) for random regular full GATE, while the sharper neighborhood-union construction is one-sided and the archived seed-union route fails at a centered Boolean radius-two operator bound.
project_justification.niche: The two-copy GATE conflict graph is bipartite, so a balanced stable set can protect both endpoint denominators without using an experiment-wide design/complement mixture. Fixed focal cardinalities also expose a covariance kernel whose dangerous common arm mode is absent by construction.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs a samplable balanced reservoir capsule, proves its exact observed-data risk certificate, derives a diagonal-scale two-arm covariance-operator bound on typical random regular graphs, and matches it with a lower bound against all procedures.

related_work: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje define the identical endpoint-\(L^2\) minimax experiment under the standard random-regular condition \(d=o(\sqrt n)\) and leave its full-GATE rate between \(d/n\) and \(d^2/n\); the focused condition \(d\to\infty\) used here is not theirs. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw provide the covariance-operator template and an \(O(\lambda(H_G)/n)\) conflict-priority guarantee, which is \(O(d^2/n)\) here. Li and Li motivate denominator protection through neighborhood unions and explicitly stop at a one-sided estimator, making two-arm cross-covariance the first changed proof step. Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 of Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang, arXiv:2210.08698v3 of 14 August 2025, supply the verified Riesz variance-operator comparison used to turn normalized exposure covariance into uniform design-based risk. Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi show how independent focal sets create logarithmic effective-sample gains under a different target and stronger response model. Perkins and Wang identify the same logarithmic balanced-stable-set scale in generic random bipartite graphs but do not address the structured GATE graph or estimator covariance. Karrer and coauthors provide the concrete large-scale global-rollout consumer for a degree-explicit precision frontier.
technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing unproved step is Theorem 1's operator bound, not stable-set size alone. The proof must control the accepted-reservoir conditioning, heterogeneous conditional inclusion probabilities, and all treated--control covariance blocks uniformly for \(d=o(\sqrt n)\). Bounding entries or the maximum codegree separately is insufficient. The embedded presolve route is to expand exact hypergeometric avoidance probabilities before taking norms, isolate the fixed-cardinality negative modes, and use a Schur-complement bound for the remaining overlap kernel. The archived Boolean-power estimate is retained only as a diagnostic and is not assumed.
honest_scope: Propositions 1--2 and Lemma 1 are finite design identities to be verified. The new open mathematical content is the random-regular covariance theorem and the all-procedure lower audit that together imply the matched frontier. Exact enumeration makes the procedure evaluable but can be exponential; Open-ended Question 1 asks whether the structured graph permits a polynomial-time estimator and observable certificate. The proposal does not claim a studentized CLT, bounded outcomes, additive interference, or that any deployed social network is uniformly random regular.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Slides 28--34 give the neighborhood-union construction, the one-sided variance theorem, the self-normalization question, and the explicit unresolved passage from the treated component to the full Horvitz--Thompson contrast.
seed_details.kernel: Use a fixed-cardinality two-arm reservoir capsule in the bipartite full-GATE conflict graph and prove that its signed normalized exposure-covariance operator is of order \(d^2/\log d\), yielding a full-GATE risk of order \(d^2/[n\log d]\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the one-sided union design and the failed centered Boolean-power estimate by a balanced pair \((A,C)\) with \(\operatorname{dist}_G(A,C)>2\), arm swapping, and a direct Schur decomposition of the signed focal-exposure covariance kernel.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for balanced independent-set GATE designs, stable-set exposure covariance, and two-copy conflict-graph randomization returned no causal paper analyzing this target--method pair; the closest mathematical work concerns balanced independent sets in generic random bipartite graphs.
adjacent_threads: KandirosHarshawSavje2026DesignBasedMinimax fixes the unrestricted benchmark and unmatched random-regular interval.

seed_details.novelty_check: No adjacent thread contains a fixed-cardinality two-arm reservoir law, its observed-data Rao--Blackwell estimator, or the claimed \(d^2/\log d\) signed covariance norm on radius-two random-regular conflict graphs.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Li and Li because their neighborhood-union assignment can simply be mixed with its complement.
seed_details.rebuttal: A design-level complement mixture creates an experiment-wide arm mode and does not control the cross-arm covariance; fixed focal cardinalities in both arms remove that mode and require a new two-arm operator argument.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The design is the decision variable and the certificate is an operator bound, so this is M13 rather than a fixed-design M12 analysis; the theorem does not assume its covariance certificate.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1 construct a priority conflict-resolution design and bound the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance through an exposure covariance operator; Section 7 asks whether its spectral rate can be improved.
seed_details.kernel: Run random sequential adsorption on the two-copy GATE conflict graph and show that the resulting maximal stable-set law has balanced inclusion density \(\asymp\log d/d^2\) and normalized covariance norm \(O(d^2/\log d)\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the one-pass importance-ordering probability calculation by the arrival-time recursion for a maximal stable set and analyze the entire covariance operator, not only its occupancy fraction.
seed_details.destination_search: Pippenger and later random-greedy work determine jamming densities on locally tree-like graphs, while the searched literature contains no covariance-operator theorem for the highly clustered two-copy graph generated by radius-two GATE conflicts.
adjacent_threads: Pippenger1989RSA derives the random-greedy occupancy fraction on regular locally tree-like graphs.

seed_details.novelty_check: The occupancy literature does not analyze a growing-degree, highly clustered two-copy graph or a normalized treated--control covariance operator, so it does not subsume the seed.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from random sequential adsorption because its jamming density is already \(\asymp\log \Delta/\Delta\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The available results concern size or root occupancy, generally at fixed degree or under local convergence; they do not control treated--control covariance, growing \(d\), or the radius-two conflict graph's many short cycles.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The named focal object is the normalized two-arm covariance kernel, not the size of a greedy independent set.

seed_details.anchor_locator: The archived core's complete-class seed and its technical limitation identify the missing passage from a stable-set upper-bound device to the unrestricted endpoint-\(L^2\) minimax game.
seed_details.kernel: Prove that the unrestricted endpoint-\(L^2\) minimax experiment equals a finite conic saddle over stable-set laws and linear representers, with recovery maps in both directions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the donor problem's sign-schedule extreme-point reduction by an ellipsoidal complete-class theorem that permits biased and nonlinear estimators before establishing strong duality.
seed_details.destination_search: Kallus gives mixed-strategy minimax design for nonnetwork experiments and Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 of Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang, arXiv:2210.08698v3 of 14 August 2025, give the relevant design-based Riesz operator comparison; no located paper proves losslessness of linear representers for this stable-set observation channel.
adjacent_threads: HarshawSavjeWang2025Riesz characterizes linear representers and compares risk with variance-operator norms without a nonlinear complete-class result.
Kallus2021OptimalRandomization gives mixed-strategy minimax design under nonnetwork outcome classes.
KandirosHarshawSavje2026DesignBasedMinimax reduces the network problem to maximal stable-set observations but leaves the exact functional implicit.
seed_details.novelty_check: None of these threads proves equality between the unrestricted nonlinear endpoint-\(L^2\) game and a finite conic stable-set saddle.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from finite-dimensional minimax duality after identifying assignments with stable sets.
seed_details.rebuttal: Nature's endpoint balls are ellipsoidal, irrelevant exposures are unrestricted, and the estimator class is nonlinear and biased, so neither compact bilinearity nor linear-estimator completeness is available without a new decision-theoretic reduction.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The iff complete-class relation supplies both directions; the proposal would not present an exponentially large program as a computational solution.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Proposition A.6 and the reductions around Lemma A.10 identify realizable maximal independent sets as the observation channel; Section 6 connects exact risk to distributions over these sets.
seed_details.kernel: Choose a balanced hard-core law on the two-copy conflict graph and certify its covariance through the Hessian of the log partition function.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace coarse conflict-graph eigenvalue control by a log-partition susceptibility bound under a balance constraint.
seed_details.destination_search: Balanced fixed-slice hard-core sampling was searched directly; Narang, Perkins, Wang, and Wee show a computational threshold that intersects the required density range on general bipartite graphs.
seed_details.red_team: The partition-function Hessian gives the desired covariance bound by standard strong spatial mixing.
seed_details.rebuttal: The density \(\log d/d^2\) lies beyond the generic uniqueness-scale argument for degree \(d^2\), and balance conditioning can induce long-range dependence.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The generic hard-core sampler would silently assume tractability in a regime where the adjacent complexity literature warns against it.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Section 5 constructs conservative confidence intervals and Section 7 states that tighter Wald inference may require tools beyond the usual Stein argument.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a design-based CLT and conservative studentization at the \(\sqrt{n\log d}/d\) normalization for a matched-rate stable-set estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the generic dependency-degree normal approximation by a martingale exposure-reveal decomposition aligned with the stable-set sampler.
seed_details.destination_search: Aronow--Samii and the conflict-graph paper give exposure-based inference, but no located result treats the matched random-regular normalization.
seed_details.red_team: A dependency-graph CLT and the published conservative variance estimator apply verbatim.
seed_details.rebuttal: At the proposed normalization, the squared-neighborhood dependency degree is too large and zero joint inclusion pairs make consistency of the published bound nonautomatic.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The design-based limit law would be derived from primitive dependence, but it is downstream of an as-yet-unproved matched design.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Section 6 formulates computational-hardness conjectures because the exact minimax functional depends on maximal independent-set structure.
seed_details.kernel: Return in polynomial time an assignment sampler, a legal estimator, and an observable constant-factor upper certificate for unrestricted full-GATE minimax risk.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace information-theoretic enumeration of stable-set distributions by a graph-computable relaxation and rounding theorem specialized to two-copy GATE conflict graphs.
seed_details.destination_search: Conflict-graph priority designs and balanced-independent-set approximation thresholds were searched; neither supplies an a posteriori ratio to unrestricted causal minimax risk.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely an implementation corollary of any attaining stable-set design.
seed_details.rebuttal: A computable certificate comparable with unrestricted risk is not implied by a sampler or an asymptotic average-case rate, but the hardness boundary makes this too broad for the first attack.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The certificate, rather than polynomial runtime alone, is the M13 optimality object.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Slides 31--33 isolate the failure of raw codegree control and ask whether increased inclusion probabilities offset covariance under intermediate neighborhood overlap.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize a uniform graph class on which one-sided normalized exposure covariance is bounded despite arbitrary codegrees, using overlap profiles rather than maximum codegree.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain inclusion denominators inside the Schur kernel instead of bounding unnormalized covariance entrywise.
seed_details.destination_search: Focused searches found the slide statement and generic covariance-optimized network designs but no full overlap-profile theorem.
seed_details.red_team: This is just a sharper proof of the one-sided slide theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: An overlap-profile condition can cover graphs excluded by the maximum-codegree hypothesis, but the one-sided target has lower consumer value than the full-GATE kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is not padded into the final shortlist because it does not close the two-arm target.

seed_details.anchor_locator: The archived review and presolve record the proved all-procedure lower edge \(d^2/[n\log(d+1)]\) and the remaining logarithmic gap.
seed_details.kernel: Strengthen the balanced-exposure Bayes lower bound to \(d^2/n\) by proving a smaller typical balanced stable-set frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the first-moment balanced packing count by a correlated second-moment or overlap-gap analysis.
seed_details.destination_search: Balanced independent-set asymptotics on random bipartite graphs show that logarithmic-size balanced sets are typical, opposing the proposed no-log strengthening.
seed_details.red_team: False because random bipartite graphs admit balanced independent sets of density proportional to \(\log \Delta/\Delta\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The two-copy graph is structured rather than a generic bipartite graph, but no evidence supports the required collapse, so the objection currently holds.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed was not retained after the destination search contradicted its motivating heuristic.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Algorithm 1, Theorem 1, and Appendix A use a greedy independent focal set and a differential-equation argument to obtain a \(n\log s/s\) effective sample size in an Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi graph.
seed_details.kernel: Prove a finite-population CLT for a direct-effect estimator under their greedy focal design when the graph degree grows.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Augment the fluid-limit size proof with a martingale CLT for the focal outcome sum under fixed potential outcomes.
seed_details.destination_search: The searched exposure-mapping literature already offers local-dependence CLTs, while the direct-effect model in the anchor imposes additional response restrictions.
seed_details.red_team: A standard finite-population sampling CLT applies after conditioning on the focal set.
seed_details.rebuttal: The graph-dependent focal selection is informative for fixed outcomes, but the resulting contribution is narrower than the full-GATE frontier and close to existing design-based CLT machinery.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The generic CLT shape risks becoming routine once the selected-set dependence is conditioned away.

literature_map.settled: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje reduce the network experiment to the exposure conflict graph and prove, for random \(d\)-regular graphs with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), the bracket \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\).
literature_map.open_boundary: Their Corollary 5.4 does not determine the random-regular full-GATE scale; the maximal-stable-set reduction does not itself identify an attaining law.

literature_map.settled: Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw give exact exposure-probability and covariance formulas for their priority design and prove a variance bound proportional to \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\).
literature_map.open_boundary: For the full-GATE conflict graph on a random regular network, the guarantee is of order \(d^2/n\); it does not exploit a balanced stable-set reservoir of size \(n\log d/d^2\).

literature_map.settled: Li and Li protect treated full-neighborhood exposures and obtain a one-sided rate under controlled codegrees.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their slides explicitly leave the two-sided Horvitz--Thompson contrast and intermediate-overlap covariance unresolved.

literature_map.settled: Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi construct a greedy independent focal set and obtain a logarithmic effective-sample gain for direct and spillover targets under a restricted exposure-response model.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their construction neither targets unrestricted ANI full GATE nor gives a two-copy signed exposure-covariance certificate.

literature_map.settled: Perkins and Wang identify balanced independent sets of density \((2+o_d(1))\log d/d\) in generic random bipartite graphs and a factor-two local-algorithm barrier.
literature_map.open_boundary: This supports the logarithmic stable-set scale but does not analyze the structured radius-two conflict graph or causal estimator covariance.

literature_map.settled: Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 of Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang, arXiv:2210.08698v3 of 14 August 2025, compare uniform design-based estimator risk with the norm of a design-induced variance operator.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their general representation does not construct a covariance-optimal network assignment or establish the random-regular operator bound.

literature_map.settled: Karrer and coauthors deploy cluster-randomized network experiments and document the precision stakes of estimating global rollout effects.
literature_map.open_boundary: That implementation literature has no unrestricted minimax sample-size benchmark as a function of network degree.

literature_checklist.author: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje
literature_checklist.one_line: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) for random \(d\)-regular graphs with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).

literature_checklist.author: Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 4.1 bounds modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by a constant times \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) and endpoint second moments.

literature_checklist.author: Li and Li
literature_checklist.venue: IMSI Recent Advances in Random Networks
literature_checklist.one_line: Slides 28--35 give a neighborhood-union design for the treated component and leave the full two-arm estimator open.

literature_checklist.author: Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 give the verified comparison between uniform design-based risk and the scaled variance-operator norm.

literature_checklist.author: Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 proves that a greedy independent focal set has size at least \(n\log s/s\) in the stated Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime.

literature_checklist.author: Perkins and Wang
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper identifies the \(\log d/d\) balanced-independent-set scale and a local-algorithm barrier in generic random bipartite graphs.

literature_checklist.author: Aronow and Samii
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper supplies the exposure-mapping Horvitz--Thompson framework and randomization variance under general interference.

literature_checklist.author: Karrer, Shi, Bhole, Goldman, Palmer, Gelman, Konutgan, and Sun
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper describes deployed cluster-randomized network experiments for global rollout effects and their bias--variance tradeoff.

literature_checklist.author: Narang, Perkins, Wang, and Wee
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper locates computational thresholds for balanced fixed-slice independent-set sampling on bounded-degree bipartite graphs.
